coordinateReferenceSystem.note: NOT WGS84. [x, y] in canonical game units, origin LOWER-LEFT, +x right, +y UP. This is the single coordinate space shared by the LevelEditor, the Simulator and the game, and by the stored level geometry. Nothing rescales: use these numbers verbatim. Map artwork is exactly 2868x2064 in this same space.

metadata.title: Siege of Charleston, 1780 - the Neck
metadata.designModel: Kingdom Rush: Frontiers stage 9 'Lost Jungle' (road terminals on all four edges knitting through a central junction web), with Forsaken Valley's slot density and Icewind Pass's folded-serpentine coverage.

designNotes.slotPlacement: 6 slots meet every strict clearance (>=139.3 to road centerline, pad clear of road). 7 'verge' slots hug the roadside with the virtual footprint overlapping the road edge by up to 30px (Kingdom Rush convention; shipped Charleston uses d 80-176, median 136, with overlaps to 59px). 4 slots encroach the HUD-corner menu-outset bands by design necessity - 17 slots plus 40% coverage cannot fit inside the strict menu-safe area (packing ceiling is ~13); shipped Charleston makes the same trade on slots 7/10/17. Every slot pad keeps >=8px clearance from the HUD occlusion rects themselves, stays inside the menu-safe rect proper, and no two pads overlap. roadInRangeAtL1 and emphasis are computed at the DB's ranged L1 tower range of 180 (towers.sql); emphasis weights road length by how many of the six lanes share it.
designNotes.portMarkers: Entrance/exit markers sit 64 units inside the play edge ON the path centerline; path polylines run ~150 units past the play edge into the bleed so enemies walk on/off screen (Charleston convention). Marker-to-mouth distances are ~214, inside the sync tool's pathWidth*2 matching radius.

properties.name: Play area
properties.note: The 1920 x 1080 gameplay viewport in canonical map units.

properties.name: Ashley River
properties.artNote: Broad tidal river filling the west bleed; the west road arrives at a ferry landing on its bank.

properties.name: Cooper River
properties.artNote: Tidal river in the northeast bleed; the east road runs down to wharves on its bank.

properties.name: Spring creek
properties.artNote: Small creek rising at the mill hairpin's spring and winding southwest into the Ashley marsh.

properties.name: Ashley marsh
properties.artNote: Impassable tidal marsh across the southwest low ground - the reason no road crosses this corner.

properties.name: Live-oak wood
properties.artNote: Dense live-oak and palmetto mass rounding the northwest corner; hides the map edge.

properties.name: Pine stand
properties.artNote: Pine stand rounding the northeast corner between the top road and the Cooper.

properties.name: Neck farms
properties.artNote: Fenced farm plots in the north-central meadow; tower pads here sit in field corners.

properties.name: Siege parallel
properties.historical: The British approached Charleston in April 1780 by formal siege, digging parallels across the Neck.
properties.artNote: Zig-zag earthwork and gabions at the wood edge, hinting at the besiegers' second parallel.

properties.name: The Hornwork
properties.historical: A brick hornwork straddled the town gate on the Charleston Neck - the city's main landward defense in 1780.
properties.artNote: Brick gate citadel below the bottom exit; the south road passes through its gate into town.

properties.name: Charleston
properties.artNote: Town rooftops and St. Michael's steeple filling the south bleed - what the defense is protecting.

properties.name: Ashley Ferry Road
properties.artNote: Rutted sandy highway from the Ashley ferry planks, running the Neck between glebe fences before it swings down through the town gate under the Hornwork's brick.

properties.name: Broad Path to the Wharves
properties.artNote: The old Broad Path carried straight over the Neck, crushed oyster shell paling to grey as it reaches the Cooper-side wharf pilings.

properties.name: Neck Road to the Town Gate
properties.artNote: The besiegers' road down the Neck, hooking around the farm orchard fence to the crossroads and down to the gate, its verges chewed by gun limbers.

properties.name: Wharf Road off the Neck
properties.artNote: Where the Neck road forks east for the wharves; hoofprints and barrel-stave litter drift toward the Cooper waterfront.

properties.name: Ashley-Side Lane
properties.artNote: The flanking lane: around the farms' west fence, back along the trunk, then down the river slope in deep wagon ruts to skirt the tidal marsh toward the gate.

properties.name: Marsh Causeway
properties.artNote: A low corduroy-and-shell causeway over the marsh margin, sagging south into the wet ground mid-run, then climbing past the mill pond to the wharves.

properties.name: Entrance 0
properties.artNote: Ashley ferry landing - the west road climbs from the river bank.

properties.name: Entrance 1
properties.artNote: Neck road - the British parallels press down the Neck from the north.

properties.name: Exit 0
properties.artNote: Town gate through the Hornwork - the defence of the city wall.

properties.name: Exit 1
properties.artNote: Cooper wharves - the waterfront batteries behind the town.

properties.name: Oak-Grove Battery
properties.artNote: Earthen gun platform tucked under the dripping live-oaks, sandbags mossy at the wood's edge; its menu bleeds over the top-left HUD.

properties.name: Second Parallel Redoubt
properties.artNote: A gabion-and-fascine redoubt left from the siege's second parallel, raw sand still bright on the parapet; menu bleeds over the HUD.

properties.name: Ferry Watch Redoubt
properties.artNote: Low sodded redoubt on the knoll above the ferry road, driftwood revetment facing the Ashley.

properties.name: Causeway Battery
properties.artNote: Timber-floored battery pad on pilings at the causeway's north verge, cattails crowding its base.

properties.name: Glebe Land Pad
properties.artNote: Mown square of church glebe land, boundary stones at its corners, bounded by a wattle fence.

properties.name: Ropewalk Yard
properties.artNote: Foundation of a burned ropewalk, long charred sill timbers and coiled hemp lying in the grass.

properties.name: Orchard Knoll
properties.artNote: A knoll of gnarled peach trees in white bloom, petals drifted against the fence rails.

properties.name: Half-Moon Battery
properties.artNote: Crescent earthwork facing the marsh where the causeway sags south, spartina grass gone gold at its lip.

properties.name: Powder Magazine
properties.artNote: Squat brick magazine mounded with turf, a plank ramp and scattered kegs at its door.

properties.name: Peach Orchard Pad
properties.artNote: Cleared circle inside a straggling peach orchard, stumps fresh-cut for fields of fire.

properties.name: Fenced Glebe Plot
properties.artNote: Inside the Neck farms: a split-rail plot of turned dark earth with a scarecrow leaning east.

properties.name: Old Apple Orchard
properties.artNote: Inside the Neck farms: a corner of old apple trees, a ladder and baskets abandoned mid-harvest.

properties.name: Race Course Green
properties.artNote: Open turf of the New Market race course, a leaning furlong post and hoof-torn grass, pines rising beyond.

properties.name: Ropewalk Head
properties.artNote: The head-house of a Cooper-side ropewalk, tar barrels and a windlass on packed shell ground.

properties.name: Wharf Battery
properties.artNote: Ship guns landed from the wharves and mounted on a plank deck, breeching ropes bolted to driven piles.

properties.name: Hornwork Glacis
properties.artNote: Bare scraped glacis east of the gate road, sloping toward the Hornwork's tabby brick just off-map.
